## End-to-End Delivery Pipeline

This is the **canonical path** for every feature — from first requirement to merged code.
Claude follows this pipeline for all work without exception.

```
Phase 1 ──► Phase 2 ──► Phase 3 ──► Phase 4 ──► Phase 5 ──► Phase 6
  BRD       Stories     Refine      Implement   PR Review   Merge & Close
 /brd      /stories    /refine      /implement  AI + Human    Human
 SM + PO     SM        SM + Leads   Developer   Tech Lead    Dev / Lead
```

**Claude always suggests the next phase after completing any phase. Never leave the user without a clear "what next".**

---

### Phase 1 — BRD Creation

**Entry condition:** Epic or Feature exists in ADO with a title and high-level description
**Command:** `/brd AB#[epic] --project "[project]" --team "[team]"`
**Exit condition:** BRD `.docx` posted to ADO; PO confirms scope in chat or ADO comment.

**Claude's next-step prompt after `/brd` completes:**
```
✅ BRD complete — posted to AB#[epic].
Next: once the PO has reviewed and confirmed scope, run:
  /stories AB#[epic] --project "[project]" --team "[team]"
```

---

### Phase 2 — Story Decomposition

**Entry condition:** PO has approved the BRD scope.
**Command:** `/stories AB#[epic] --project "[project]" --team "[team]"`
**Exit condition:** All stories created in ADO and linked to Epic; traceability matrix posted; stories assigned to a sprint.

**Claude's next-step prompt after `/stories` completes:**
```
✅ [N] stories created and linked to AB#[epic].
Next: assign stories to the sprint in ADO, then run:
  /refine --project "[project]" --team "[team]"
```

---

### Phase 3 — Refinement & Quality Gate

**Entry condition:** Stories assigned to sprint.
**Commands (run in order):**
1. `/refine --project "[project]" --team "[team]"` — batch RAG score all sprint stories
2. `/check AB#[id] --project "[project]" --team "[team]"` — fix each 🟡 or 🔴 story

**Exit condition:** Every sprint story scores 🟢 Green on all 8 dimensions.

---

### Phase 4 — Implementation

**Entry condition:** Story scores 🟢 Green on `/check`; story state is "To Do" or "Ready".
**Command:** `/implement AB#[id] --project "[project]" --team "[team]"`
**Exit condition:** PR opened, all tests passing, CI pipeline green, story in "In Code Review".

**Claude's next-step prompt after PR is raised:**
```
✅ PR raised — AB#[id] is now In Code Review.
Next: assign [Tech Lead] as reviewer on the PR.
Once they approve and all CI checks pass, tell me "merged" and I'll close the story.
```

---

### Phase 5 — Code Review

**Human requirement:** At least **1 human approval** required — Claude's review alone is never sufficient to merge.
**Exit condition:** Claude review passed, ≥1 human approved, all CI checks green, no unresolved threads.

---

### Phase 6 — Merge & Close

**Action:** Human merges the PR → tells Claude **"merged"** in chat.
**What Claude does:** Verifies ACs → sets story Done → checks siblings → asks before closing Epic.

---

### Pipeline phase gates

| Gate | Condition required | If not met — Claude stops and says |
|------|-------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Phase 1 → 2 | PO has approved BRD scope | "Has the PO approved this BRD? Reply 'yes' to run /stories." |
| Phase 3 → 4 | Story scores 🟢 on `/check` | "AB#[id] is ⚠️/❌. Fix the flagged issues first, or use `--skip-check`." |
| Phase 4 → 6 | ≥1 human approved the PR | Claude will not mark story Done until user says "merged". |
| Any phase | Story state = "Waiting for Requirements" | "AB#[id] is blocked. Resolve the blocker before proceeding." |

---

### Blocked story handling (OI-xxx pattern)

When a story depends on an unresolved external item:
1. Document the blocker in the work item: `⚠️ BLOCKED — [OI-xxx]: [description]. Owner: [name].`
2. Set story state to **On Hold**.
3. During `/refine`, blocked stories are flagged and excluded from capacity.
4. Claude will not run `/implement` on a blocked story without explicit user confirmation.

---

## Work Classification & Scenario Playbook

Every work item that reaches Phase 4 must be classified before any code is written. Claude reads the story title, description, and AC to determine the type, then follows the matching playbook below.

### Step 1 — Classify the work

| Dimension | Options |
|-----------|---------|
| **Layer** | Frontend · Backend · Full-stack |
| **Nature** | New (greenfield) · Modify existing · Bug fix · Code quality / Refactor |

---

### Playbook A — New Frontend Page (Greenfield)

1. Check for an existing route file — add the new route there, do not create a parallel routing system.
2. Check for a shared layout/template/wrapper — reuse it exactly as other pages do.
3. **If a Figma link exists in the story:** fetch the design via Figma MCP before writing any UI code. Extract screen names, field labels, validation rules, navigation flows, empty/error/loading states.
4. Scaffold in this order: route → page component → child components → custom hook (if logic exceeds ~30 lines) → unit tests.
5. Follow existing naming conventions and folder structure exactly — do not introduce new patterns.
6. Every new component must be covered by at least one test.

---

### Playbook B — Modify Existing Frontend Page/Component

1. **ALWAYS read the existing file(s) in full before writing a single line.**
2. Glob/Grep for all files that import or reference the component being changed — understand the blast radius.
3. Make the **smallest change** that satisfies the AC. Do not refactor, clean up, or improve surrounding code unless the story explicitly asks for it.
4. Preserve existing prop interfaces — extend, never break. If a prop type must change, flag it as a breaking change in the PR description.
5. Run existing tests after your changes. Add tests only for new behaviour being introduced.

---

### Playbook C — New Backend API Endpoint

1. Read existing route files to understand the established pattern (file naming, middleware chain, validation approach, error handling).
2. Follow the same service-layer and repository pattern already in use — do not introduce a new architectural pattern.
3. Add input validation at the route boundary.
4. Add: a unit test for the service layer + an integration test for the route.
5. Document the endpoint in the PR description: method, path, auth requirement, request shape, response shape, error codes.

---

### Playbook D — Modify Existing Backend Service/Route

1. **ALWAYS read the existing route, service, and any repository/helper files before writing.**
2. Grep for all callers of the function or method being changed — check for unintended side-effects.
3. Make targeted changes only. Do not reorganise the file or rename unrelated symbols.
4. Run the full test suite for the affected module after changes.
5. If the change alters a public API shape, state explicitly in the PR description whether it is a **breaking** or **non-breaking** change.

---

### Playbook E — Bug Fix (Frontend or Backend)

1. **Reproduce first.** Identify the exact file and line where the bug originates. Do not guess.
2. Read the surrounding code to understand *why* the bug exists.
3. Write the **minimal fix**. Do not add unrelated improvements.
4. Add a regression test that would have caught this bug.
5. PR description must include: **Root cause:** [X]. **Fix:** [Y]. **Regression test:** [Z].

---

### Playbook F — Code Quality / Refactor

1. Scope is strictly limited to what the story or task describes. Do not expand beyond it.
2. **No observable behaviour changes.** If a refactor accidentally alters behaviour, flag it and stop.
3. Run the full test suite before starting and after finishing. If any test breaks, it is a blocking issue.
4. PR description must include before/after metrics where measurable.

---

### Playbook G — Full-Stack Story (Touches Both Layers)

1. **Read the backend first.** Understand the API contract the frontend will consume.
2. If the backend endpoint does **not yet exist**: implement backend → tests → document the API shape → then implement frontend.
3. If the backend endpoint **already exists**: read it fully before writing any frontend code.
4. Deliver both layers in a single branch and single PR unless the story explicitly splits them.
5. PR description must contain a short API contract summary: endpoint, method, request, response, auth.

---

## Codebase Exploration Protocol

**For any Modify, Bug Fix, Code Quality, or Full-Stack work — run this sequence before writing any code.**

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | **Locate the entry point** — find the exact file containing the component, route, or service to be changed. |
| 2 | **Read the full file** — never make changes based on a partial read. |
| 3 | **Trace dependencies** — Grep for all imports of that file; understand what depends on it. |
| 4 | **Find the tests** — locate the corresponding test file(s); understand what is already covered. |
| 5 | **Check types/interfaces** — if TypeScript, find the type definitions the file uses. |
| 6 | **Note environment variables** — identify any `process.env` reads; never hardcode them in changes. |

For **greenfield (Playbook A or C)**: steps 3–6 still apply to understand the existing patterns you must follow.

## Coding standards

Apply these standards in all code review and generation tasks.

### General
- Functions must have a single responsibility and stay under 50 lines.
- No magic numbers — use named constants.
- All public methods/functions must have corresponding unit tests.
- Error handling must be explicit — no swallowed exceptions or unhandled promise rejections.
- Use `async/await` over raw Promises. Never mix callbacks and promises.
- Prefer Azure-native services over third-party alternatives (e.g. Azure Key Vault for secrets, Azure Storage for blobs, Azure Service Bus for messaging).

### React (frontend)
- Prefer functional components with hooks over class components.
- Use `React.memo`, `useMemo`, and `useCallback` where appropriate to prevent unnecessary re-renders.
- Keep components focused — extract logic into custom hooks when a component exceeds ~100 lines.
- Props must be typed (TypeScript interfaces or PropTypes).

### Node.js (backend)
- Use ES modules (`import/export`) over CommonJS (`require`).
- Express route handlers must use error middleware — never let errors go unhandled.
- All Azure service interactions should use the official `@azure/*` SDK packages.
- Environment variables for secrets — never hardcode connection strings or keys.

### Naming
- Variables and functions: camelCase
- React components: PascalCase
- Constants: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
- Files: kebab-case (React components may use PascalCase filenames)

### Pull requests
- PRs must reference an ADO work item (e.g. `AB#1234` in the title or description).
- PRs should be small — prefer < 400 lines changed.
- All CI checks must pass before merge.
- At least one human approval required after Claude review passes.

## Slash commands

| Command | What it does | Pipeline phase | Next step |

| `/sprint` | Scrum Master board — all sprint items by status & assignee | Planning | — |
| `/standup` | Standup prep notes (before) or Teams summary (after, `--post` to auto-send) | Daily | — |
| `/velocity` | Multi-sprint velocity trends; `--export ppt` or `--export pdf` | Reporting | — |

## Story point estimation model

The team uses Claude Code for AI-assisted development. Estimates reflect **human effort** (review, guidance, validation), not raw coding time.

| Points | Human Hours (AI-assisted) | When to use |
|--------|--------------------------|-------------|
| 1pt    | ~2h                      | Trivial — single file, obvious change |
| 2pt    | ~3h                      | Small — 1–2 files, straightforward logic |
| 3pt    | ~6h                      | Moderate — clear requirements, known patterns |
| 5pt    | ~16h                     | Complex — multiple files, design decisions |
| 8pt    | ~30h                     | Large — cross-cutting, architectural thought (max per sprint) |
| 13pt   | must split               | Exceeds sprint capacity even with AI — split first |

**Valid scale: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13.** Off-scale values (4, 6, 7, 10–12) require re-estimation.

Capacity formula: `team members × days available × 6h ÷ 4 = sprint capacity (pts)`
Use `--ratio 6` on `/refine` or `/check` to revert to the pre-AI baseline.

## Work item state management

Follow these rules on every `/implement` run, without exception.

### When starting a story
1. Set the story state to **In Progress** immediately before writing any code.
2. Set all child items (Subtasks, Tasks) linked to the story to **In Progress** at the same time.

### When finishing a story (PR created)
1. Set the story state to **In Code Review**.
2. Set all child items to **In Code Review**.

### When a PR is merged (user confirms "merged")
1. Verify the story's acceptance criteria are fully met by the implementation — do not close on assumption.
2. Only if all ACs are satisfied: set the story to **Done**.
3. Set all child items to **Done** at the same time.
4. If the story has a parent (BR, Epic), check whether ALL sibling stories are now Done. If so, ask the user before closing the parent — do not auto-close it.

### State transition summary

| Event | Story state | Child item states |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| `/implement` starts | In Progress | In Progress |
| PR opened | In Code Review | In Code Review |
| PR merged + ACs verified | Done | Done |

## Post-PR lifecycle

### Reviewer assignment (default rules)

Claude suggests the appropriate reviewer immediately after raising the PR:

| PR type | Default reviewer |
|---------|-----------------|
| Frontend (React, CSS, HTML) | Frontend Lead |
| Backend (Node.js, routes, services) | Backend Lead |
| Full-stack / cross-cutting | Scrum Master |
| QA / test-only | QA Lead |

### Merge conditions checklist

| Condition | Who verifies |
|-----------|-------------|
| CI pipeline green (build + tests) | ADO / automated |
| Claude PR review passed (no 🔴 blockers) | Claude (`ado-pr-reviewer`) |
| ≥ 1 human approval | Tech Lead (human) |
| No unresolved comment threads | Reviewer + Author |
| PR references AB#[id] in title or description | Author |

### Post-merge sequence

When the user says "merged":
1. **Verify ACs** — Confirm every AC is covered before closing.
2. **Close story + children** — Story → Done; all child Tasks/Subtasks → Done.
3. **Check siblings** — If all siblings under the Epic are Done, ask: *"Shall I close the Epic?"*
4. **Regression reminder** — Prompt to run the full test suite on `{{MAIN_BRANCH}}`.
5. **Next story prompt** — Suggest the next highest-priority story in the sprint.

## Things Claude should NOT do

### Source control
- Never commit directly to `{{MAIN_BRANCH}}` or `release/*` — always create a branch and PR.
- Never force-push to `{{MAIN_BRANCH}}` — warn the user and stop if asked.
- Never delete branches, repos, or pipelines without explicit user confirmation.

### Work items & ADO
- Never delete work items, pipelines, or repos without explicit confirmation.
- Never close a parent work item (Epic, Feature, BR) without explicit user confirmation — even if all children are Done.
- Never move a story to Done without the user saying "merged" and AC verification passing.
- Never update a work item field without showing the before/after and getting confirmation.

### Security & secrets
- Never store secrets, API keys, connection strings, or tokens in code or comments.
- Never modify pipeline variable groups that contain production secrets.
- Never hardcode environment-specific values — always use environment variables.

### Pipeline gates
- Never run `/implement` on a story that scores 🔴 Red on `/check`, unless `--skip-check` is used and the user provides a documented reason.
- Never skip the Phase 1 → 2 gate (PO BRD approval) — do not run `/stories` until the user confirms PO approval.
- Never auto-merge a PR or mark a story Done based on Claude's own review alone — human approval is always required.
- Never skip CI pipeline failures silently — always surface the failure to the user.

### Roles & reviews
- Never approve or complete a PR — that requires a human reviewer.
- Never assign Claude itself as a PR reviewer in ADO.
- Never send standup messages or Teams posts without explicit `--post` confirmation from the user.
